claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density.
The baseline alloy has less than 5% room-temperature ductility and is brittle.
Adding 2-5 at% Si or Al alters atomic-size and electronic interactions and thereby drives Laves-phase nucleation in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Hf, Zr, and Ti have atomic radii of approximately 1.59-1.60 Å, whereas Si and Al have radii of approximately 1.17-1.43 Å.
A large-to-small atomic-radius ratio of approximately 1.22 is typical for an AB2 Laves phase.
Heat treatment at 800-1000 °C for 10-100 hours can precipitate a secondary Laves phase in the modified alloy.
The secondary phase will be a C15 or C14 Laves intermetallic arranged as a reticulated network at grain boundaries and within grains.
The matrix will retain its BCC structure after Laves-phase precipitation.
A reticulated Laves-phase network will act as a physical barrier that deflects or bridges cracks.
Crack deflection and bridging by the Laves network will increase fracture toughness and room-temperature ductility.
The Laves precipitates will produce precipitation hardening and increase yield strength.
The proposed heterogeneous phase structure will improve strength-ductility synergy and overcome the usual trade-off.
Adding Si or Al will leave density comparable to the baseline or slightly decrease it because these elements are lighter than Hf and Mo.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 200-400 MPa, from approximately 800 MPa to 1000-1200 MPa.
The intervention will increase uniform elongation from less than 5% to more than 15% under room-temperature compression.
The modified alloy will have improved specific strength.
The fracture surface will show crack deflection and intergranular fracture along the Laves network.
Ductility improvement requires a continuous or semi-continuous Laves network and may be limited if the phase forms only isolated particles.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis first predicts a moderate density increase, then states that density may decrease or remain similar and predicts comparable or slightly decreased density. The uncertainty field leaves the direction unresolved.
